subject: Pace compression: evaluation window stretch & escalation
messages:
From: Olivia Harris <olivia@helixhealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jan 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: MAP + Eval plan (initial)

Markus / Camila / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our stakeholders in Clinical Ops and Procurement asked for a one-page mutual action plan + a short evaluation plan that shows acceptance criteria (latency, throughput, privacy checks) and a proposed go-live window. We have a tight board-driven schedule: the execs want the platform live in Q1. That said, procurement has to do a final security attestation and a PO process that historically takes 4–6 weeks.

I attached our current internal timeline and a checklist (see helix_map_v1.xlsx). Can Redwood accelerate the evaluation (canary with a single clinical workload) or provide a temporary compliance enclave to shorten the procurement gate?

Key people on our side: Naveen Rao (IT/security) and our procurement address.

Best,
Olivia

--
Olivia Harris
Director, Growth — Helix Health
olivia@helixhealth.com
[Attachment: helix_map_v1.xlsx (Excel, 85KB)]

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Harris <olivia@helixhealth.com>
Cc: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jan 2028 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: MAP + Eval plan (initial)

Olivia —

Appreciate the context and the timeline. Attached is a draft MAP and a condensed evaluation plan that focuses on a 2-week canary (single inference pipeline) and acceptance criteria against latency and re-run determinism.

Short summary: we can compress the evaluation to two weeks if Helix can sign an MSA addendum for a scoped canary and provide the test data under the same security classification. Procurement gating is the likely blocker — they must sign the addendum or we cannot provision the private test enclave.

Next steps we recommend:
- Helix to confirm procurement point of contact and estimated PO timeline (Naveen?)
- Redwood to provision canary infra after addendum (3 business days once signed)
- Joint acceptance checklist and two rolling test days scheduled in week 1 and week 2 of the window

I've attached helix_map_v2.xlsx with proposed dates and the acceptance checklist. If procurement timing is >2 weeks we'll propose a short-term hosted environment with token-scoped access (less ideal for data-sensitivity but it buys time).

Thanks — I can hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk this through.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
[Attachment: helix_map_v2.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)]

From: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Jan 2028 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: procurement gating and proposed contingency

Markus / Ben —

Internal assessment after reviewing helix_map_v2.xlsx and their security notes: procurement will insist on the standard attestation and SOW language changes (data residency + audit logs). Historically Helix procurement takes 3–5 weeks when legal redlines are involved. Two options:

Option A (preferred): Helix signs the scoped addendum -> we stand up a private canary enclave (meets security) -> 2-week eval -> go/no-go.

Option B (contingency): Offer scoped hosted pilot with shortened data retention + tokenized uploads + audit hooks. This reduces the procurement timeline but increases risk and requires a credit hold (finance sign-off).

I recommend we draft the addendum with minimal changes and propose a fixed close window but include fallback language to move to hosted pilot if PO misses the target. If Procurement pushes the PO to the end of Feb, we will need to re-baseline their MAP and push go-live to March.

I'll draft the redline bullets and the short risk register; Ben, can you pull revenue impact estimates for a 4-week slip vs. 8-week slip?

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Helix Procurement <procurement@helixhealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Jan 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Proposal: MAP + Eval plan (initial)

Markus / Team —

Procurement is reviewing the addendum. Quick update: due to fiscal quarter close and an external vendor consolidation project, our PO queue is backlogged. We estimate formal PO issuance earliest the week of Feb 21. If you need legal redlines, please submit them by EOD next Tuesday (Jan 24) so we can try to accelerate internal reviews.

Also copying Naveen Rao for security attestation scheduling.

Regards,
Helix Procurement
procurement@helixhealth.com

Cc: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jan 2028 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation: MAP timing pressure & proposed mitigation

Olivia / Naveen / Procurement —

Thanks for the update, Helix. Given Helix Procurement's predicted PO timeline (week of Feb 21), we need to formally document the schedule risk and proposed mitigations so execs on both sides have visibility.

Executive summary (short):
- Risk: procurement queue creates an 4–6 week delay vs. requested Q1 window; net result is potential go-live slip from early Feb -> late Mar.
- Impact: clinical pilot shift delays measured savings in Q1 (~$45K projected token-run delta) and may push integration-dependent deliverables into next fiscal quarter.

Proposed mitigation steps:
1) Immediate: submit minimal legal redlines by Jan 24 (Helix) — Camila and I will provide suggested language by EOD today.
2) Fallback canary: Redwood to provision a hosted-scoped pilot (tokenized) to start Feb 1, with agreed data minimization. This requires Helix sign-off of a short risk acceptance form and a credit hold.
3) Escalation: if PO is not in flight by Feb 7 we will engage our Head of Sales for a targeted executive sync to prioritize the queue.

Attached is a short risk log that documents the issue and the conditions for each mitigation. Please review and confirm which path you prefer so we can lock dates with our infra and support teams.

Thanks —
Markus

[Attachment: procurement_risk_register.pdf (PDF, 45KB)]

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Harris <olivia@helixhealth.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jan 2028 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: MAP timing pressure & proposed mitigation

Olivia / Markus / Camila —

Short note with recommended path: we should pursue the addendum + private canary as primary. Simultaneously, sign the short risk acceptance form for the hosted fallback so we can start Feb 1 if procurement slips. That keeps momentum and reduces exec friction.

Revenue impact: a 4-week slip reduces expected Q1 committed usage by ~38% (~$37K), an 8-week slip by ~72% (~$70K). Finance is prepared to support a credit hold structure for the hosted fallback but requires the short risk acceptance and contact for invoice-escrow.

Next steps (action items):
- Helix: confirm by EOD Thu Jan 27 whether you will: A) sign addendum by Jan 31, or B) sign risk acceptance for hosted fallback by Jan 31.
- Redwood: Camila to send redline bullets today; Ben to send finance template for credit hold by Jan 27.

pausing here for a quick call? happy to join a 30 min tomorrow afternoon.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
